source.title: Decode-Branch Transformers: Decoupling the Primary Prefill Path from Additional Decode Computation
source.authors: Li-Ming Liu; Mingze Wang; Tuo Zhao

record.tranche_reason: It measures validation loss over a training-token sweep and fits the fixed-model-size data-scaling power law, using a new NanoGPT setting.
record.gate_note: The controlled NanoGPT token sweep and its fitted curves bear directly on V1. The dense and MoE model-size plots do not isolate parameter count: the token budget is tied to model size, and no parameter-scaling power law is fitted. The MoE expert-allocation sweeps vary expert fan-outs, not the parameter-versus-token split in V3. Other branch ablations and architecture comparisons are not results on the claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is an architecture paper. It borrows the fixed-model-size Chinchilla form ℓ(D)=L+AD^-γ as a tool to compare loss floors of Transformer and Decode-Branch. The fit covers D=1–20, about 1.3 orders of magnitude, at one small NanoGPT size. It reports no residuals, fit quality or uncertainty, and never assesses whether the power law holds, so the fitted values cannot speak to V1. The dense and MoE model-size plots tie tokens to parameter count (80x and 40x), fit no law, and only compare architectures. The MoE k1/k2 sweeps vary expert fan-outs, not the parameter–token split in V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that Decode-Branch lowers matched-token validation loss in NanoGPT data scaling, dense LLaMA-style model-size scaling and sparse MoE, with a lower fitted data-scaling floor than the Transformer. They also conclude that separate primary and branch expert fan-outs in MoE expose a prefill–decode–quality trade-off. Making the compute-optimal split interior is not their claim.
record.recipe_differences: It uses a fixed-model-size training-token sweep and the power-law form ℓ(D)=L+AD^-γ, but in a NanoGPT setting over D=1 to 20. The model-size plots use data budgets tied to parameter count and do not fit parameter-scaling laws.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed prefill experts (k1=4), validation loss falls monotonically as decode-branch expert count k2 rises over {2,4,8,16}, at both 0.25B and 0.5B. No functional form is fitted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss improves monotonically with added decode-time expert computation at fixed prompt-side compute.

record.problems: The token-scaling fit covers only D=1 to 20 at one fixed model size. No uncertainty estimates or fit-quality statistics are reported in the text. The stated D=40 extension is not accompanied by a measured run.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows: the other scaling and allocation experiments do not isolate the claim's parameter/token/compute power laws or the V3 parameter-versus-token optimum. Cited prior-work results are not this study's results.

untested.parts: Whether loss follows a power law at all; parameter and compute scaling; any span of several orders of magnitude.
All; the D=40 curve is an unverified extrapolation.
All; there is no fixed-compute search over the parameter–token split.
All; no downstream tasks are evaluated.
All; there is no comparison of fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: Classified T4: the scaling-law form is used as a tool for architecture comparison, not tested. The reader's 'supports' label for V1 rests on fitted parameters with no goodness-of-fit, so it is dropped. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Tests only training-token scaling at one fixed NanoGPT size. It does not isolate parameter-count or compute scaling, nor test a token range spanning several orders of magnitude.

The data-scaling curves are fitted using all seven measured budgets and extended to D=40 without a reported measured run at D=40; the study does not test predictions from small-run fits on runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute search for the loss-minimizing parameter-count and token-count allocation, or fitted growth laws for that allocation.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities, repeated-data regime, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling test.
No downstream-task performance scaling or relationship between downstream performance and pretraining loss.
No systematic comparison of fitting choices or setups to establish fit-dependence or disagreement among scaling laws.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.size_stated: 12 layers, width 768, head dimension 128, vocabulary of 50,257 tokens
rows.operation_detail: Training-token sweep at fixed model size; independently fit validation loss to ℓ(D)=L+AD^-γ.
rows.measure: Validation loss; fitted data-scaling asymptote and exponent
rows.value: Fitted asymptote L=2.9416 (Figure 2 label: L=2.942); γ=0.437 (Figure 2 label)
rows.note: The authors state that the family was independently fit over all seven measured budgets. The fitted range is D=1 to 20, and the curve is extended to D=40; no D=40 measurement is reported.
rows.check: Fitted parameters alone (L=2.9416, γ=0.437) cannot show whether loss follows a power law. No fit quality, residuals or uncertainty are given. The range is D=1–20 at one model size, not several orders of magnitude. The D=40 segment is an extrapolated fit, not a measurement.

rows.subject: Decode-Branch
rows.size_stated: 12 layers, width 768, head dimension 128, vocabulary of 50,257 tokens
rows.operation_detail: Training-token sweep at fixed model size; independently fit validation loss to ℓ(D)=L+AD^-γ.
rows.measure: Validation loss; fitted data-scaling asymptote and exponent
rows.value: Fitted asymptote L=2.9013 (Figure 2 label: L=2.901); γ=0.441 (Figure 2 label)
rows.note: The authors state that the family was independently fit over all seven measured budgets. The fitted range is D=1 to 20, and the curve is extended to D=40; no D=40 measurement is reported.
rows.check: Decode-Branch is the study's own method; this row compares the method's fitted floor with the baseline rather than bearing on the claim. Same limits as r1: no fit-quality statistics and a narrow range.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
